title: How often Jelly wrote; grandmother's view of his work
summary: He wrote monthly; she did not want him telling night stories and rejected his tin pan band.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: About how often did your brother write to you, would you say?

About once a month to me. And he didn't write to my grandmother for a long time. And I told him one time I was writing letters in ink, and I had just learned to use ink. And it was so blotted because my mare was crying. Mm-hmm.
Yeah, well, we're just about out of this tape. I mean, if you don't feel like talking any more about it, it's all right. No, but I didn't want him to hate my grandmother.
She was so good to earth. Well, yes.
Of course, if he didn't in the way, I guess she sort of sent him away from home, so he...

But, you know, the thing was this, you want him to respect the girl and not come in... Yeah. ...and tell his experiences of the night before to my uncle, you know? Mm-hmm. And, and I mean, some of those things were shady, I guess. Yeah. But, I mean, when Jelly would come in as a child, and I remember when I was about six years old, and he'd come down here with some kind of, she called it a tin pan band, you know, Tin Allen.
Yeah. Lord, and, you know, people looked down on South African people. Yeah, at that time, yeah.
And my grandmother's from the old school, she just wouldn't accept that.
